text:
detour answers with a 302 instead of proxying because the user wanted the client to contact the backend directly, so detour never carries the traffic. Two consequences follow from this and neither is visible in the code:

Rejected alternative: Caddy alone does this job with about five lines of config (reverse_proxy with lb_policy first, health_uri and health_interval) and zero code. It was rejected only because it proxies rather than redirecting. If the requirement ever relaxes to allow proxying, delete this program and use Caddy. Nothing off the shelf does a health-checked 302, which is the sole reason this code exists.

Strict failover rather than round-robin was chosen by the user specifically so that only one backend URL is public at a time. Round-robin would publish the whole backend list to anyone watching redirects. Do not 'improve' this into round-robin or weighted balancing.

A 302 gives no signal when a real request fails, because failures happen between the client and the backend. The periodic health check is therefore the only liveness source, and there is no possible retry or circuit breaker. This was discussed and accepted.

Deployment context for detour, as stated by the user:

Target is Dokku, with Caddy in front terminating TLS. detour itself only ever speaks plain HTTP and must never grow TLS termination.

Configuration is environment variables rather than the TOML file originally planned. The switch was made because Dokku configures apps with 'dokku config:set', which needs no persistent storage mount and no SSH to the host to change a backend. The config is only three keys, so a file bought nothing. This also removed the single external dependency and left the program on the standard library alone.

The original use case was a pool of public Nitter instances, which is where the working name 'nitproxy' came from. The project was renamed to 'detour' because nothing in it is Nitter specific. Backends must be publicly reachable, since clients are redirected straight to them; a private backend cannot work with a 302 at all.
